sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match or one word).

questions.q: (a) In a region of constant potential, what is the electric field? (b) What is the shape of the equipotential surfaces of a single isolated charge?
questions.answer:
(a) Zero (E = −dV/dr).
(b) Concentric spheres centred on the charge.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The SI unit of capacitance is ______. (b) The energy stored in a capacitor is ______.
State True or False: (a) Two equipotential surfaces can intersect. (b) The electric field is perpendicular to an equipotential surface.
Complete: a 2 µF capacitor is charged to 12 V. (a) Charge = ______. (b) Energy stored = ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) Capacitors in ______ have their capacitances added. (b) A dielectric of constant K increases the capacitance ______ times.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is an equipotential surface? Why can two equipotential surfaces not intersect?
questions.answer:
A surface on which every point has the same potential; no work is done moving a charge along it.
If two intersected, the common point would have two different potentials and two field directions, which is impossible.

questions.q: A capacitor is kept connected to a battery of voltage V. How does the energy stored change when the plate separation is doubled?
questions.answer: C = ε₀A/d halves when d is doubled. With V fixed, U = ½CV² also halves.

questions.q: The Q–V graphs of two capacitors X and Y are straight lines, X being steeper. Which stores more energy at the same voltage?
questions.answer: The slope Q/V = C, so X has the larger capacitance. U = ½CV², so at the same V, X stores more energy.

questions.q: Write the expression for the energy stored in a capacitor in three forms.
questions.answer: U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV. It is stored in the electric field between the plates.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A 2 µF air capacitor is charged to 12 V and the source removed. A slab of dielectric constant 5 then fills the space. Find the ratio of the energies stored before and after.
questions.answer:
Before: U₁ = ½CV² = ½ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 144 = 1.44 × 10⁻⁴ J.
Q stays constant; C becomes 5 × 2 = 10 µF.
After: U₂ = Q²/2C' = U₁/5 = 2.88 × 10⁻⁵ J.
U₁ : U₂ = 5 : 1 (energy is drawn into the slab).

questions.q: Derive the expression for the energy stored in a parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance C charged to potential V.
questions.answer:
While charging, at charge q the p.d. is q/C. Adding dq needs work dW = (q/C) dq.
Total work W = ∫₀^Q (q/C) dq = Q²/2C.
With Q = CV: U = ½CV² = ½QV, stored in the field between the plates.

questions.q: Three capacitors of 2 µF, 3 µF and 6 µF are connected (a) in series and (b) in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance in each case.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor and show how a dielectric changes it. How do the charge, p.d., field and energy change when a dielectric slab is inserted (a) with the battery connected and (b) after disconnecting the battery?
questions.answer:
Plates of area A, separation d, charge ±Q: σ = Q/A, E = σ/ε₀, V = Ed = Qd/ε₀A, so C = Q/V = ε₀A/d. With a dielectric filling the gap, E is reduced K times, so C = Kε₀A/d.
(a) Battery connected (V fixed): C → KC; Q → KQ; E = V/d unchanged; U = ½CV² → KU.
(b) Battery disconnected (Q fixed): C → KC; V → V/K; E → E/K; U = Q²/2C → U/K.

questions.q: Define electric potential and potential difference. Derive the potential at a point due to a point charge, and state the relation between field and potential.
questions.answer:
Potential at a point: the work done per unit positive charge in bringing a test charge from infinity to the point, V = W/q₀ (volt = J/C). Potential difference between A and B is W_AB/q₀.
Point charge q: the field at distance x is kq/x². The work against it from ∞ to r is W = −∫∞^r (kq/x²) q₀ dx = kqq₀/r, so V = q/4πε₀r.
Relation: E = −dV/dr — the field points in the direction of decreasing potential, and E = 0 where V is constant.
